slides.title: Professionals run a drill
slides.text: When an incident lands, professionals do not improvise. They run a drill with four moves: contain, preserve, report, recover. Your hand-sized version of it starts now.
slides.alt: Spot the trick, Pro style: the lesson card names the levers. Rush, prizes, and asking for your mailbox key.

focus.cue: Spot the trick: where the drill gets its cards
Rush, prizes, key asks, strangers: know the signs

slides.title: Contain the damage
slides.text: Contain means stop the bleeding first. Leave the fake page, and change the key from a clean device you trust, not from the screen that may have tricked you.
slides.alt: A trick wearing a bank's name: for your safety, it says, confirm your mailbox key and your birthday.

focus.cue: The trick card wearing a bank's name
The badge says unknown sender: contain it there

slides.title: Preserve the evidence
slides.text: Preserve means keep the proof: screenshots, the message, the time it arrived. Do not delete in embarrassment. Evidence is what lets adults and platforms act, and speed beats embarrassment, twice over.
slides.alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

focus.cue: The faked sender name on the card
Preserve it: the whole card is the evidence

slides.title: Report, then recover
slides.text: Report to a trusted adult, your school and the platform. Then recover: a fresh passphrase on the hit account, and everywhere it was reused. That is the separate-keys lesson from Unit 2, paying off.
slides.alt: A real message for once: your teacher, a sender you know, about the field trip forms. Nothing to tap, no rush.

focus.cue: The real message from a sender you know
Report, then recover: the buttons wait below

slides.title: Run the whole drill
slides.text: You tapped a faked sender's link and typed your passphrase before the doubt arrived. Run the drill in order.
steps: Contain: leave the page, change the key from a clean device
Preserve: screenshot the page and note the time
Recover: new passphrase everywhere it was reused
slides.alt: A parcel trick: a delivery you never ordered is waiting, and a small fee must be paid within two hours.

focus.cue: Asks for money, two hours to act: run the drill

slides.title: The one-line log
slides.text: Afterwards, Defenders write one line: what happened, what the drill caught, what changes. Incidents are tuition. The log is how the next Defender pays less for the same lesson.
slides.alt: A fan club card that knows too much: your dog's name and your birthday, learned from your public profile.

focus.cue: The fan club card that knows too much
They know your dog and your birthday: log that

words.means: something that has gone wrong with security or safety
to stop an incident spreading or doing more harm
to keep evidence safe and unchanged
to restore accounts and services to safe working order

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Trick Inbox and play the Boss Round. Treat every message as a live incident: contain, preserve, report, recover.
slides.alt: Trick Inbox, the Boss Round at Pro: a letter claiming an account will be deleted waits in the inbox, one clue found and one still hiding.

focus.cue: The Boss Round message, with one clue found
